utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we hear the testimony of the next witness unless there are any other preliminaries we will move into closed session. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did have a preliminary. I wanted to inquire --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- the day before yesterday I made an application with respect to RM070. I was wondering whether the Chamber has had a chance to deliberate and make a decision on that application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will inform you later this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move into closed session, unknown for how long. Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President and Your Honours, everyone in and around the courtroom. I just wanted to raise with respect to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not yet in closed session until Madam Registrar has confirmed so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness RM254, you'll first be examined by Ms. Hasan. You'll find Ms. Hasan to your right. Ms. Hasan is counsel for the Prosecution. Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we call up 65 ter 29069, please, and this should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, without readings out loud what you see on the screen before you, could you confirm that the name and date of birth recorded there is accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 65 ter 29069 into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives P1688, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, just to remind myself and to remind you to pause between question and answer and to speak at a good pace so that the interpreters can keep up with our words. Do you recall providing a statement to the ICTY on 18th of August in 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we see 65 ter 29011 on the screen without it being broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, take a look at this page. Could you confirm whether or not you are identified here on this cover page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if I could ask you to look to the bottom right-hand corner of the English version of this document. Do you recognise your signature there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HASAN
utterances.text: And if I could ask to turn to page 5 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise your signature on this page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, we've met over the last few days, and we have discussed a number of corrections that you wish to make to this statement. Do you recall those discussions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd ask that 65 ter 29081 be displayed and again not be broadcast. Your Honours, this is a document that's a list of corrections that the witness made to his statement over the last couple days, and it was not on our 65 ter list originally as it was just created, and I ask that we get leave to add it to the 65 ter list and use it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Ivetic? For the record, Mr. Ivetic nodded no. Madam Registrar -- first, Ms. Hasan, leave is granted to add 65 ter 29081 to your 65 ter list. And may I take it that you are going to tender that as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, I will. I just have a few questions for the witness relating to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so. Please put questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, do you recall reviewing this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And do the corrections therein accurately reflect the corrections and clarifications you wish to make to your 1996 ICTY witness statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, I don't intend to go over all of these, but I do want to ask you about one of those corrections, and this, in fact, relates to your statement where you've identified seeing certain individuals. It might be helpful to call up that, and for this purpose, I'm going to call up 65 ter 29080.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, just so that this is clear, what I have done is I've taken the witness statement and numbered the paragraphs. So this version of the witness statement with the numbered paragraphs accompanies the corrections so that they can be tied together more easily. So if we could turn to page 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, perhaps a general observation. We always attached to the 92 ter motions we find unnumbered statements. Later always the numbers are referred to, whereas the Chamber then has the unnumbered versions. Perhaps it would be far more convenient for everyone if you already numbered the statements, perhaps indicating that you have done so after the statement was taken in the attachment to the 92 ter motions. That would save a lot of confusion. But this is unrelated specifically to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So, Witness, what's numbered here as paragraph 13 -- and if we could turn also to the same page in the B/C/S version. And this shouldn't be broadcast. I'm not sure if it is or isn't at the moment, but ... Now, Witness, here you recall naming a number of individuals that you saw. Do you see that there in paragraph 13, and in the B/C/S version it's the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, do you recall these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us how it is that you know them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew them. These are my neighbours from the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us when was the last time that you saw these individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw those individuals the last time when we were arrested, when we were driven towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please speak a little louder and well in the microphone so the interpreters can hear you well?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So you saw them in Burnice; is that correct? Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you see them at the meadow that you were taken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you see these individuals in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So is it correct, then, that you wish to amend your statement, that paragraph of the statement, so that the last time you saw these individuals named here was at the meadow and not at Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could go briefly into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, the information that you've provided in your statement taking into account these clarifications and corrections that you have made, is it true and accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if you were asked today about those same matters would you provide the same answers subject to those clarifications and corrections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd offer the witness statement dated 18 August, 1996, and perhaps I would suggest we go with the one with the numbered paragraphs which is 65 ter 29081 into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 29081 receives number P1689, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And it's also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence under seal. And now the corrections, I take it, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's 65 ter 29080.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe it's 29081.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's correct. Thank you. 29081.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for the assistance, Mr. Ivetic. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we already assigned a number to 29081.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore -- and -- yes. Did we admit it already? Yes, it was admitted, so therefore there is no need to admit it again, Ms. Hasan. Let me --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I think the error comes from me. I initially referred to the statement as 29081 when it should have about 29080 with the corrections being 29081.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I'm lost.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar will now assign a number to 65 ter 29080.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Which receives number P1690, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1690 is admitted into evidence under seal. Ms. Hasan, we are at the time where we need a break, but before we do so, we move into closed session so that the witness can leave the courtroom, and we'll resume in closed session at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. If you'd bear with us for a second and have some patience. Before we continue and being in open session, Mr. Stojanovic, I would like to address you briefly, and I do this on behalf of the Trial Chamber which is unanimous in this respect. This Chamber has allowed Mr. Ivetic to examine witnesses despite the fact that he's not appointed counsel or co-counsel, assigned counsel or co-counsel. As a member of the Defence team, Mr. Ivetic acts in disrespect under your supervision and your responsibility. In your presence, Mr. Ivetic misbehaved today in more than one respect. One of the questions he did put to the witness was unfair, and the knowledge Mr. Ivetic later showed to have made it also clear that he should have been aware of the inappropriateness of this question. Further, Mr. Ivetic used a tone which was disproportionally aggressive and triumphant and the same can be said of his gestures. He finally ignored the way in which the Presiding Judge had stated he wanted to deal with the two cases where there was a dispute between Prosecution and Defence as to whether and what protective measures had been applied. He instead wanted to pursue the approach he apparently preferred and did not hesitate to interrupt the Presiding Judge repeatedly to this end. Mr. Stojanovic, it would have been appropriate for you to intervene as counsel present to put an end to the misconduct of Mr. Ivetic. Counsel responsible for the conduct of -- in court of Mr. Ivetic as a member of the Defence team further should be aware -- when I say "counsel," I refer to you as co-counsel and Mr. Lukic as counsel, should be aware that if this behaviour would be repeated, that there may come a point where the Chamber will have to reconsider the leave it granted for this team member, not being counsel or being co-counsel, to examine witnesses at trial. I leave it to that, and we will now continue to hear the testimony of this witness. Ms. Hasan, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Before putting further questions, Your Honours, I will read a brief summary of the witness's prior evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: After Srebrenica fell, the witness and his father went to Jaglici where they left towards Buljim and Kamenica. They were ambushed near Kamenica and the witness was separated from his father. He continued on his own through the woods and eventually descended to a village he spotted. On his way down, he was captured by Serb soldiers and taken near a warehouse. He saw several other Serb soldiers escorting ten other captured men. The Serb soldiers executed these men and wounded a 17-year-old boy outside of this warehouse. While fetching water for one of the Serb soldiers, the witness managed to escape into the woods. The witness made his way to Burnice village where he recalls spending the night and looking for food the next day and then being surrounded by Serb soldiers. These soldiers escorted the men they captured in a column from the hills to the asphalt road leading to Konjevic Polje. The prisoners were taken to a meadow where their hands were tied with wire and they were forced to lie down. A short, overweight brown-haired soldier who appeared to be in charge asked the witness how old he was. The witness said he was 13 years old. The soldier in charge cut the wire on his hands and took the witness to a bus where he saw three other young boys. The witness and the other boys were taken to the military barracks in Bratunac where they were interrogated and filmed. On the following day, four Serb soldiers transported them in a white UNPROFOR UN vehicle to the Zvornik police station. They were then taken to Kalesija where they were released. That concludes the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, how old were you in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was 16.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, the Judges have read your statement, so they know -- are aware of the events that you went through. Can you tell us, did those events have a traumatic effect on you, and, if so, in what way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. To this day I have trauma. I cannot sleep at night.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we see Exhibit P1690, which is the witness -- witness's statement, and if that -- that shouldn't be broadcast. And if we could in the English turn to page 3, paragraph 6. And that's the same in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, as that comes up, in that paragraph 6 you discuss a soldier who asked you to fetch some water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So it's page 3, paragraph 6 in both versions. And if you take a look at the bottom of paragraph 6 you say as you went to get water: "I went to leave my rifle on the ground, but he said to me not to leave my rifle on the ground ...," and it goes on. Now, when you were captured near the warehouse in the Kravica area, were you carrying a rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So where did you get that rifle from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were given that rifle by those Serb soldiers. I don't know exactly how many of us there were. They gave us those rifles and told us to walk ahead of them. They took us down below, not far from there. They said that the Bosnian Army should come by there, and I know that they mention the commander, Ejub Golic, and if we did not shoot at them, that they would shoot us and kill us.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we turn to page 4 in the statement. It's at page 3 in the B/C/S version, paragraph 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, in that paragraph you discuss your arrival at Burnice village, and you say: "Our group of ten arrived at Burnice village. There were about 500 others. I stayed the night there and spent the next day looking for food. At about 6.00 p.m. on 15 July 1995, we were surrounded by Serbs." Witness, that date that is provided there, is that a precise date or is it an approximation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It's just an approximation. I didn't know what date it was or what time it was. I didn't know any of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, when you were in Burnice village and the Serbs -- Serbs surrounded and captured you, how did you come to the conclusion that there were 500 of you that were captured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes. When we were captured, we were made to go up to a meadow, there we were lined up, and they counted us while swearing at us, saying, You're Balijas mother, and so on. He said, Because of 500 of you Balijas, you were so loud the whole of Serbia had to move.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And as you were being escorted by the soldiers there Burnice to the meadow by the asphalt road, did anything happen to the men in the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. One of our men, Muslims, tried to escape, and a Serb soldier shot him on the spot, dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So you were then taken to a meadow near an asphalt road. As best you can, can you describe for us where the meadow was located.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes. As far as I can remember and to this day every time I pass by there I have confirmed again and again that this meadow is near Lolici. Below the road there is a water fountain there that had been built in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So the water fountain, where was it relative to the meadow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This water fountain is above the road, whereas we were below the asphalt road. We were lower down. And this water fountain was on the other side of the asphalt road above -- above the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did that fountain exist at the time you were taken to the meadow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you describe the fountain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes. It was a water fountain, a water tap, really. There was a pipe, a water pipe, coming out of this water fountain. It was made of concrete.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned the village of Lolici. Can you give us a bit more -- can you orient us a little bit more as to where it was? Was it in the village, near the village, between which villages? Can you help us out there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this village, Lolici, there is another village there, Pervani, we were closer to Pervani -- or rather, I'm not sure but I believe that we were closer to Pervani there at the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you say that when you arrived at this meadow, this field, there were 500 corpses lying all over it. How did you arrive at that figure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I was so scared and it seemed to me as if there were 500 bodies, but there were probably around a hundred. They were scattered all over the meadow, because they had been shot dead before.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can we briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, could I ask one question. One of your previous answer was that there was a water fountain. You then said below the road, whereas you said later on the upper side of the road "that had been built in the meantime." What do you refer to if you say "in the meantime?" The time between what and what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I meant this: After the war it was just built upon, but the water pipe was there, and it was above the road, as I've already said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much for this clarification. We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could take a look at this statement again, and at page 5, paragraph 13. Witness, you describe in this paragraph that the morning after you arrived at the Bratunac barracks that you were interrogated and then taken out to play football with the Chetniks. Can you tell us a little bit more about those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We were detained there, and then they took us out, outside the barracks, and we had to play ball with the Serbs, and then they filmed that with a video camera. And then they took us back inside, and then again they took us out and let us see the TV programme that they had filmed earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just to follow up on a couple of things. When you say, "We had to --we had to play ball with the Serbs," what do you me by that? Were you forced? Did you go there voluntarily? Can you explain that for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes. We couldn't say no. They didn't force us, but we wouldn't dare say no. We were afraid for our own safety. We thought that if we refused that they would just shoot us dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did they tell you anything about why they were filming you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. As far as I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: When you were driven from Bratunac in a white UN vehicle, what did you think was going to happen to you at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes. We couldn't really believe that they would let us go to the free territory. During that entire trip we thought that they were taking us somewhere where they would kill us, like they killed everybody else, that we could see for ourselves. That's all we could think of. We weren't thinking of any future survival or our families or anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: When you were eventually taken to Kalesija and released, do you have any recollection today about when you arrived there, the date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. No. I couldn't even believe that I had crossed over into Kalesija. And as for the dates, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hasan. Before the Defence will start its cross-examination, Judge Fluegge has a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. We have still the document on the screen. It should not be broadcast. Paragraph 13, I would like to ask you for a clarification. You are telling there about the bus where you were in, and you were driven to Bratunac, and then you are saying: "As I was walking out of the bus, I heard a Serb soldier from the trucks ask the commander what to do with the people. The commander was outside, and he replied to take them to the Vuk Karadzic school where the killing place was." Especially the last part of that I don't fully understand. Did the commander say that killing will take place there, or how did you know that that was a killing place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no. That's what he said, Take them to the Vuk Karadzic school. You know where the killing take place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: These were the words of the commander. He told the Serb soldier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And you heard that yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to start with some background questions, and to do so I would ask that we go into private session to protect your identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, I wish to go over some parts of your Rule 92 ter statement that has been tendered by the Prosecution in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As a preliminary matter, every time we pull it up can we please be sure not to broadcast the same, and I'd like to pull up P1690 under seal, and if we can turn to page 2 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And while we wait for that, sir, I should ask you first if at the time of making this statement in 1996 did you have the ability to read or speak the English language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how about now? Do you speak or read English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now I want to focus on the second paragraph at the top, and here you say that: "Some soldiers came to our village on 11 July 1995 to say that Srebrenica had fallen and that we must leave the area. I heard aeroplanes and two strikes in the morning of that day. Our family had to split up. My mother, younger brother and sister went towards Potocari, and me and my father, born 1995 in Srebrenica, left with the Bosnian Army in the direction of Buljim." Now, I want to first clarify with you the soldiers that came to your village and told you that you must leave the area because Srebrenica had fallen, are we talking about Armija BiH soldiers here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. BiH Army soldiers who were going from Srebrenica and who passed through our village, they told us that Srebrenica had fallen and that we had to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is it also correct that these Armija BiH soldiers that told you that you had to go also told you that women and children were to go to the UN compound in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, could you clarify for us whether it was the Armija BiH or UNPROFOR that instructed the women and children to go to the compound in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the soldiers came there were some stories, but nobody from UNPROFOR came to our village to go down there, but there was just this talk that we should go to UNPROFOR, but we did not believe that. Only when our soldiers came from Srebrenica and said that Srebrenica had fallen, only then did we believe it, and then our women and children set off towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt the cross-examination. Could we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, at the time that you -- that you and your father set out with the BiH Army for Buljim, were either of you armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean me and my father?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. None of us had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can return to your Rule 92 statement, 1906 under seal, and not broadcast the same. And if we can return to page 2, I want to look at portions of the third paragraph with you. And, sir, here in the third paragraph, it's about the fourth line in English and it's about the fourth and fifth lines in the B/C/S of this paragraph, it says: "In the morning we moved on through Buljim towards Kamenica. We got to a hill above Kamenica and sat down to rest. We were separated by brigades to rest. Mine was," and you list the name of the brigade, "and there were about 1.000 of us in my group." So I want to ask you, sir, this brigade that you mentioned, was it within the structure of the Armija BiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How did you become a member of this brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I did not become a member of the brigade. Us civilians had to go with the army. Children over 16, for example, did not dare to go to Potocari because the children were being separated as well. So we had to go through the woods with our parents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in relation to the 1.000 men that were part of your group, am I correct that a certain number of them had weapons in their possession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Most of them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you were talking about 1.000 men. As I read here, it says, "And there were about 1.000 of us in my group." It doesn't state whether these are men, and now you've just told us that there were children also over 16 who accompanying people, accompanying this --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. You're absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, the 1.000 of you that were part of the group, am I correct that a certain number of those individuals had weapons in their possession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were those who were carrying weapons. This was the B and H Army members who were walking ahead. We were walking in the back, civilians, without weapons, as well as civilians who were unprepared for battle, civilians and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- and with respect to those persons that were armed as part of this group, is it correct that in addition to hunting rifles they also had automatic rifles and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to take a look at 65 ter number 29071 but not broadcast the same to the public. And if we could look at page 17 in the English and page 24 in the B/C/S. And it's the second half of the page in the English, whereas in the B/C/S it's at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you're talking about the first ambush in Kamenica, and I'd like to discuss with you that, if I may. First, I'll read for you what is recorded in this transcript: "Defence counsel: Was that first ambush in Kamenica? "The Witness: The first ambush was immediately here when we left from Buljim, but I wasn't in that ambush. I had already passed that ambush. I came across the second ambush in Kamenica. "Defence counsel: Was anyone killed in that first ambush? "The witness: Yes. "Defence counsel: From the column, yes? "The witness: Yes. "Defence counsel: What happened to those bodies? "The witness: Well those bodies remained there in those places where they were killed. "Defence counsel: All right. And tell me, in relation to the place where you were in the column, where were those armed men? "The witness: Those armed men always went first. Those who had weapons went first. Those of us who didn't have weapons went behind, and that is how it went. "Defence counsel: Were there any people at the end of the column with weapons? "The witness: There were a few hunting rifles and that was it." Now, is this part that I've just read to you both truthful and accurate as to the facts that are contained therein such that you would so testify today if I were to ask you the same questions? Perhaps I can break it up. Sir, the part that I've read for you, is it both truthful and accurate as to the facts cited therein?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you so testify today the same way if I were to ask you the same questions about these same facts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now I want to return to your Rule 92 ter statement, P1690, and again the same should not be broadcast, and again we need page 2 in both languages. And again, in paragraph 3, approximately the sixth and seventh lines in the B/C/S, you say: "During the night of 13 July, 1996," which has been corrected to 1995, "we were ambushed. A beech tree was felled and then the ambush started from all sides. All types of fire were used: Rifles, bombs, hand grenades, mines, and war agents. When we all dispersed, I was split up from my father and I did not see him until after that. I've not heard of him since then. After the first ambush and around dawn," and then you continue. So I want to ask you: This description that I've just read from your 92 ter statement, does it in fact relate to the first ambush that you were not involved in according to the testimony we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That was a different ambush where this tree fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's focus on the part that I read to you from your 92 ter statement. Were you personally present and did you personally experience that particular ambush which is -- which is detailed there with the beech tree falling, all types of fire being used: Rifles, bombs, hand grenades, mines and war agents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was there, but I don't remember the war agents, but I remember everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And so -- and so in this paragraph when it says: "After the first ambush and around dawn a helicopter was above, and through a megaphone it told people that there was food for them and to come out into the open from the woods," is this first ambush talking about this incident that you were present for, or is it talking about the incident that we looked at in your other testimony that you were not present for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes. I don't remember the helicopters or anything like that. I don't remember them flying over us. I tried to remember that, but, really, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir. We'll get to the helicopters in a little bit. If we look at the middle of this paragraph again that's on the screen, paragraph 3, you describe how Chetniks infiltrated the column and pretended to be wounded, and you saw one lure a person to help them and then stab them. And I want to ask you first: Was this Chetnik who was pretending to be wounded lying down or on his back at the time that he lured the person to come over to assist him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember if he was lying down or not, but I know that there were many such cases in the woods, people saying that they knew the way as guides and then they would take 10 or 15 people with them, and then those people would never return.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm talking now specifically about the incident that you've identified with the Chetnik that was wounded and lured someone and then stabbed them. Do you recall if that was the only such instance of that which you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall that. All I know is that throughout our passage through the woods people said that we should not be going anywhere with unknown people because Chetniks had infiltrated themselves among us wearing regular clothing like us and that during the night they would lure people away or stab them or lead them to ambushes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me see if I can clarify this. Did you in fact actually see anyone lured over by a Chetnik pretending to be wounded and then to be stabbed by that same Chetnik as is recorded in your Rule 92 ter statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall seeing anything like that. It's possible that I did see something like that, but I do not remember. It's possible that I do not remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did anyone ever call you over to ask you to dress a wound that you thought was a Chetnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did that person appear to be armed that called you over to ask you to dress a wound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They were wearing civilian clothing, just lying there, but I did not dare go up to them because of all of those things that I heard that were going on. I ran away from that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now I would like to turn to the next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one clarifying question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you do remember that a Chetnik called you over to dress a wound but that you fled. You said he was in civilian clothes. Now, how do you know that he was a Chetnik, or was it just that you feared he might be a Chetnik which was luring you into a dangerous situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was afraid that that was a Chetnik, because there was talk that Chetniks had infiltrated the woods and that they were using these tricks and deceit, so I did not dare approach the person, and I ran away from that place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you were never able to establish whether he really was a Chetnik or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I think we're close to the point where we would take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When we could do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we first turn into closed session in order to allow the witness to leave the courtroom, and we will resume at a quarter past 12.00, again in closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if we can turn to - I apologise - the next page of your Rule 92 ter statement. So it's the next page in both languages. We're looking at the middle of the paragraph that's been marked 5. Now, here, sir, towards the end of the paragraph number 5 of the statement that you have confirmed as being truthful and accurate and that has been admitted into evidence under seal, you say as follows: "The soldiers who caught me had red bands around their arms with something saying 'Yugoslavia' on them." Could you describe for me your recollection of these bands that the soldiers had on their arms. Is this, in fact, something that you recall seeing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Some had regular simple red bands, while others had this band on which it said "Yugoslavia." Now, whether this was just written out in some ink or something, I don't know, but it said "Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And with respect to this paragraph - we'll stay here again - you identify an incident where some persons were shot at the warehouse, and you say as follows: "The Serbs escorting the other captured ten people then executed them all, except one kid of about 17 years who was wounded. Before they got to the warehouse the Serb soldiers lined them up in front of the warehouse but not right by it, at a right angle to the warehouse. The soldiers stood about 10 metres away and three soldiers opened fire with a burst from their automatic rifles. I have drawn a sketch map at Annex B to show where the soldiers and the people stood in relation to the warehouse as well as showing where the woods were from which I had come. They were left there in a heap, and the other Serb soldiers said this would happen to us if we tried to escape. They took the kid who was wounded and put him by the side of the road. They did not dress his wound, and he himself did not dare to dress it. He was just there whining. I do not know the names of any who were killed or of the kid wounded or of the Serb soldiers who did the killing. The Serb soldiers had dark green camouflage uniforms on, no hats, and looked just normal." Now, in relation to this incident, we've already clarified that in fact you did know the person, the kid who was wounded. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is it your testimony that they left this kid by the side of the road whining?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not by the road. They took him behind a hangar, behind the green building. He was moaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I to take it from this that they did not -- that they did not attempt to dress his wounds or seek to have someone else dress his wounds?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No. A Serb soldier just said, Why did you wound this kid? He's not to blame for anything. And these two other soldiers picked him up and carried him behind this warehouse, behind the green building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can take a look at 65 ter number 29070, and page 14 of the same in English and page 17 of the B/C/S but not broadcast the same to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'd like to start at line 19 of the same, and if you can follow along, sir. Here you identify the person who was wounded, and you say as follows: "He got wounded there, and I don't know what happened to him later. "Q. Can you tell me how he not wounded? Can you give us some details?" And then you answered -- hold on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "A Serb soldier pointed his rifle at him and wounded him on the legs, and then he said, 'This child needs his wounds to be dressed.' And then two of them took him behind the warehouse and I don't know what happened to him. I've never seen him since." Is this prior testimony that I've read out for you truthful and accurate as to these facts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you answer the same way today subject to the solemn declaration to tell the truth if we were to ask you these same questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. About this youth who was wounded, I know that he was wounded there and that he was carried behind the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can just look briefly at number 29071 in e-court, again not broadcasting the same to the public. And in that document I will be needing page 9 in English at the middle of the page, and page 12 in the B/C/S at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, I'd like to read for you what is recorded here, although I will omit references to the name of the person who was wounded: "The prosecutor: Did you recognise any people you knew, any friends there? "The witness: Yes. "The prosecutor: Who did you recognise? "The witness: I recognised my schoolmate," and then you name him, "who was wounded there in this group -- in that group and remained wounded in Kravica. "The prosecutor: How old was...," and then he says the name. "The witness: Well, he was my schoolmate. We were in the same grade, so we were the same generation. "The prosecutor: How was ..." And now we need to turn to the next page in the B/C/S: "The witness: He was 16 years old." And let me just stop it right here. Was the person who was wounded 16 or 17 years, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure, but we were classmates, schoolmates. Whether he was 16 or 17, I'm not sure, but I know that we were in the same grade and that we were the same generation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that clarification. I'd like to now continue from where we left off: "The prosecutor: How was he wounded? "The witness: He was wounded in the legs by a burst of shots and then they yelled, 'Help him.' "The prosecutor: You pointed to the area of the knees. "The witness: Yes. "The prosecutor: You want to say that he was shot in that area? "The witness: Yes, in that area in the area of the knees, legs. He was wounded there because they shot him in the legs and he fell. "The prosecutor: And did you see where the others were shot? "The witness: I didn't. "The prosecutor: You just saw them shooting at them? "The witness: Yes and then. "The prosecutor: Did you see the others fall? "The witness: Yes, he was wounded and then they said 'The child needs help,' and then two of their soldiers came from somewhere and took that boy and took him behind this -- behind this building and that boy never appeared again." First of all, sir, this selection that I've read, does it truthfully and accurately depict the facts as you know them about this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you so testify again today subject to the solemn declaration to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. With respect to what happened in Kravica, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you say that they yelled, "Help him," who was it who yelled, "Help him"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the Serb soldier said. He said, The child should be helped. He's not to blame for anything, and you shouldn't have wounded him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can look at 65 ter number 29070, page 21 of the English and page 24 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Witness, again I'll be reading for you to follow along. You can also follow along the B/C/S beginning at line 14 of the page that is now on the left of your screen. And I believe this is in relation to your escape from Kravica and going to Burnice village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And it starts at line 9 in the English. The question asked was: "What happened after you escaped? What did you do then?" And you answer as follows: "I ran to the woods, and I found some ... some of our soldiers who were in the forest. They started shooting after me when they saw me running, but nobody hit me. Nobody ... no bullet got me, so I managed to get out unscathed." Sir, is this answer that I've read out from the -- from this other proceeding both truthful and accurate as to your recollection of the facts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you so testify again today if asked the same questions the same way subject to the solemn declaration to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, only while I was fleeing, when I got to the water to pour some water for myself I found a girl there some 13 -- between 13 and 15 years of age whose throat had been slit, and that's when I decided to run. I thought, Well, I better be -- I better be hit by a bullet rather than my throat slit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get to that. Now, were the Serbs shooting at you at the time that you ran into these persons that you identify as "our soldiers"? Is that a proper understanding of this testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. While I was running across this meadow and as I got into the woods, they noticed that I was fleeing, and then they open -- they started shooting after me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Who's the "they"? That's what I'm trying to determine, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, those were the Serbs shooting at us. While I was running and getting away they shot at me. They opened fire at me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And so the persons that you describe as "our soldiers" did not fire upon you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And by "our soldiers," are you referring to Armija BiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This other proceeding, without mentioning the name of it, were you testifying in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, today in P1689, a list of corrections that the Prosecution gave to us for your -- for your statement, in relation to this -- in relation to these persons that you joined up with in the forest described at paragraph 9 of your 92 ter statement, say that: "The witness clarified that they did not wear uniforms, looked exhausted and were hungry. He did not know whether they were BiH Army members or civilians, but they were -- but that they were able-bodied men." So I have to ask you now, sir: Did you believe them to be Armija BiH soldiers as you testified in your own language in this other proceeding, or did you not know them to be Armija BiH soldiers as has been presented to us by the Prosecution in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, I didn't know that they were soldiers of the BiH Army, because they didn't have a camouflage uniform, just like we didn't. They were going hungry and thirsty, going through the woods like us, and maybe these were just the men who were in the rear who then remained there, but we didn't have anything to eat. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we can return to the document that's on our screens, and it's -- it's on the same page in the English. It's on the B/C/S, the bottom of the page and the top of the next. Starting at line 15 in the English you were asked: "... escape. Where did you next go? Did you go ... did you ... I'll leave at that. Where did you next go when you escaped? /inaudible/stick in your mind about what happened next? "To the Burnice village. That's where I went. "... there? And you answered: "There along the road I saw many bodies of those who had been killed. I saw them all over the crop fields in Burnice village on my way to Burnice, and when I reached Burnice I found many of our troops and the civilians who had gathered in the Burnice village. We stayed in Burnice in a house where we just laid down to rest. We were hungry. We were tired. We were exhausted. We didn't know where to go from that point onwards, because those were just logistics forces. We didn't know the area, and we didn't know where to go to next. We had no food to eat, so we just spent some time there. And then Serb soldiers attacked us, attacked the village. They just surrounded the village without bullet fired. They surrounded the village and took us prisoners." Now, first I have to ask you: Is this account that I have read back to you truthful and accurate as to these events at Burnice village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you so testify the same way today under the obligations of the solemn declaration if the same questions were asked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As far as Burnice concerned, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And as far as Burnice is concerned, can we take from this that the Serbs captured you and the others in the village without having fired a single shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can return briefly to your Rule 92 ter statement, P1690 under seal and not broadcast the same, and if we can look at page 4 in the English and then in B/C/S it's page 3 at the very bottom. And it's in relation to the paragraph 9, and in the B/C/S it's the very last -- let me see. It's at the beginning of the paragraph, so it's paragraph 9, which reads as follows, sir: "I met up with some men from the Bosnian Army and joined with them. We made our way to Burnice and Pobudje. Our group of ten arrived at Burnice village where there were about 500 others. I stayed the night there and spent the next day looking for food. At about 6.00 p.m. on 15 July [Realtime transcript read in error "June"] 1995 we were surrounded by Serbs. The Serbs were firing ..., "and at this point we have to go to the next page in B/C/S, "The Serbs were firing into the air and squeezing the encirclement smaller and smaller. I tried to hide in the attic of a house with two others but dogs found us there. The Serbs were dressed with green military sweaters with black armbands with Yugoslavia written on them. There were many dogs which were held back with chains by the handlers who were dressed the same." Now, could you explain for us, sir, you just told us that the Serbs captured you without firing a single shot. So why does your Rule 92 ter statement say that the Serbs were firing into the air?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did capture some of us without a bullet being fired. However, because the others would not surrender they opened fire, so that even those who had been hiding in houses they were forced to get out of the houses, come out.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how many days were you in Burnice? Is the recollection here accurate that it was the 15th of June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I can't recall the dates. This is an approximation as I've already said. I can't recall the day or the date when this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I apologise. I misspoke. I said "June," I meant to say "July." Does that change your answer any, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you identified that the number of persons was 500, and today you -- I think you indicated that the Serbs counted you in a garden after you surrendered. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We got that information from them. I didn't even know how many of us there were, but until they said it, they said there were 500 of us, and they were swearing at us, swearing our Balijas mother, our -- 500 of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you -- did you eat anything at all during the time period that you were in the woods or that you were at Burnice village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We ate snails and unripe apples. They were completely unripe, green apples, and snails. Although I cannot remember all the details, I know it was horrible to have to eat that, but we just had to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was this second capture at Burnice also something that you remember very vividly, that you had a strong sense of horror about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you ever forget that second capture at Burnice village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to look at the statement that you gave to the Bosnian AID, Agency for Documentation and Investigation, in June of 1997 which was taken approximately a year after the ICTY statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could we please have 1D1095 in e-court and could we please not broadcast the same. And there we see the date and the entity it was given to, and can we please have the last page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, directing your attention to the B/C/S original on the left side of the screen, do you see your signature there on the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you see above your signature the lines that say: "I have nothing else to state. I listened to the statement being dictated aloud to me. I also took part in its formulation, and I am ready to repeat it before a Court, which I hereby confirm with my signature." Do you recall reading and understanding this before signing the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It's just that it's been many years since then, and you can forget a lot of things since that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. And if we go to the -- first of all, am I -- can I presume that this was conducted in -- in the B/C/S language, in the Bosnian language, this interview and the taking of this statement by this agency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to the bottom -- pardon me, to the middle of -- strike that. The second page in English, at the bottom, and the middle of page 2 in the B/C/S original.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at the bottom of the page in English you talk about incident that you just indicated at the fountain with the girl. We'll get back to that. If we can move to the next page in the English, and at the top, sir, I read for you as follows: "I pulled myself together a bit and realised that I was not at home but, rather, that the Chetniks had sent me to bring some water. I immediately decided to run away. I threw away the rifle, crossed the Kravicka Rijeka and started running towards the woods. They probably heard or saw me running and started shooting in my direction. They did not hit me, and I ran deep into the woods where I came across several people I did not know. I wandered for another ten days through the woods with those people --" I apologise. I don't know if there's something ... may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "... I ran deep into the woods where I came across several people I did not know. I wandered for another ten days through the woods with those people, coming across dead bodies of which I did not recognise any. "On 22 July 1995 we crossed over to the free territory of Kalesija municipality." Now, sir, is this selection from your statement from 1997 truthful and accurate such that you would so testify again the same way today if asked about these same events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I don't remember that. All I know is that I threw away the rifle, and when I saw that girl with her throat slit, I remember that, and I know that I was looking for my house. I asked for some water. I was completely lost from fear, and then my memory then came back what I was looking for, what I was doing there, and then I started to run away.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me -- let me focus on what you've said now. So is it your testimony you still had the rifle with you and you through it away when you saw the girl at the fountain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really don't know if I threw away the rifle or not. I was very scared after I saw that girl who had just had her throat slashed. She was still twitching. So I don't know if I had the rifle, if I threw it away there. I really cannot remember this anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the question I have for you is in relation to this statement that you gave one year after the ICTY statement. This statement has absolutely no reference to Burnice or the second time that you say you were captured. Can you confirm that you did not tell this agency, AID, about this second capture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. No one asked me, and I didn't speak about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, the document signed says, "I have nothing else to state." Did you not, in fact, have the capture and the time you spend at Burnice to talk about? Did you not remember it at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They didn't ask me or question me anymore. They put questions to me, and I replied and that's how it went.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, I would tender this document which is 1D1095 under seal as the next available exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1095 receives number D321, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And in the absence of any objections, is admitted into evidence under seal. Mr. Ivetic, could you give us an indication as to timing?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At the start of my examination I intended to go 2.5 hours, perhaps two hours and forty minutes with this witness. I do not know how much time we've already used up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will inquire with Madam Registrar, but could you give us an indication as to how long you think you still need.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think based on my questions that I am on track to complete the examination within that time period that I had -- that I had indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which would mean that most likely you would not finish today. Is that -- could you see whether you could focus so much on what seems to be most important and see whether you could try to finish within the next session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will try, but I don't think I can, Your Honour. We have a Rule 92 ter statement that's been admitted into evidence for which as we see every point that I'm raising --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm happy that you're willing to try, Mr. Ivetic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can turn to 65 ter number 29071, page 21 in the English, page 28 in the B/C/S. And again we should not broadcast the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Here, sir, and it's the middle of the page in the B/C/S, you were questioned about this exact same AID statement from 1997 and about the time period that you stated therein that you were wandering through the woods, and you state as follows -- first you say when you were asked from defence counsel: "Well, now I claim that on that occasion you didn't say literally anything about escaping in front of that warehouse, being recaptured, taken to Bratunac and then released after that. "The witness: Well, yes. When I gave that statement they just asked me questions and they did not ask me that question at all, and I didn't tell them about it. And --" Let me take it part by part. Do you confirm that to be truthful and accurate, that part I've just read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember that part at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then let me -- let me short-circuit it by just asking you this part here. At the tail end of -- it's down at the end of the page, you were asked about the time period that you spent in the woods, and you said: "Maybe even ten days passed in the woods or eight days or five days, and then I was captured in Burnice. "Defence counsel: So you think that it's possible that this is true and that after escaping in front of the warehouse you wandered ten more days through the woods before you were captured? "The witness: It's possible. I don't remember the exact day whether I was captured today in Burnice or tomorrow or the day after tomorrow. I can't remember that." Do you still stand by this as being accurate and truthful as the amount of time that passed between leaving Kravica and the capture in Burnice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I don't remember how long it was. Was it one day, two days, five days? I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can have 1D1097 in e-court, and this also should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I think you'll see, sir, that this is another statement that you gave to another entity, the SIPA police, known as the Bosnian State Protection Investigative Agency, and is dated 2009. And if we look at the first page of the original, is that your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the second page of the document in both languages. Item 2 is a confirmation that you understood the language using the interview. Is that your signature affirming the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we skip ahead to page 3 in English and page 3 in the B/C/S. We have the conditions at item 9 saying that you cannot withhold any information. Item 10 states that you were cautioned about giving a false statement being a crime punishable under the relevant statute. And if we go to the next page, which is page 4. Is that -- is that your signature affirming knowledge and acknowledging the foregoing cautions having been given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to go through some parts of the statement with you. Let's start with paragraph 4. I don't know if we can -- that's on both. There we go. It says here that you were 14 years old on 11 July 1995. Was that the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I was 16, but I had said that I was 14 when I was captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you understand and appreciate that this document you were preparing in 2009 with the SIPA was a legal document that you were giving answers for?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, let's try to focus on the substance. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that because you had previously given false information about your age you felt you had to keep up the prior story to be consistent, even though it was in fact false and untrue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This was not false information. False information is not the killing of innocent people that took place in Kravica. The rest can just be just an omission due to the fact that I cannot remember. As for what happened in Kravica, the killing of those people, the killing of the people on the road, that is not a lie. No one can say that that is a lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can have number 29071 in e-court, and again not broadcast the same, and page 34 of the same in English, page 47 in B/C/S. It's at the middle of the page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And to try and short-circuit this, I will preface by saying they're talking about the same statement given to SIPA, and I'll skip ahead to the part where you were asked by Defence counsel: "Defence counsel: What was the reason that you didn't also tell investigator Muris Brkic the truth here about how old you were then?" Here on page 4, in item 4, you say: "I was 14 years old at the time." "The witness: Well, I said 14 because I had given a statement before and I thought let it stay 14 because I knew that I had said that I was supposedly 14. "Defence counsel: Yes, but you were warned that you must say the truth. "The witness: Yes. "Defence counsel: Why didn't you say it then? "The witness: And I said that I was 14, but I wasn't 14. I was 16. "Defence counsel: No. I'm asking you why you told Muris Brkic then that you were 14 when it -- a simple calculation shows that you're 16. What was the reason then that you didn't say the truth about your age? "The witness: There was nothing to hide there. It's possible that there was a misunderstanding. That I didn't say -- "Defence counsel: You think that it's a misunderstanding? "The witness: Nothing else. There was no reason to hide anything." Now, I want to ask you, sir, to clarify for us: Did you give an incorrect age to the investigator of SIPA because you wanted it to be consistent with the prior statement when you said it was 14 or because you had a misunderstanding with the investigator? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There was a misunderstanding with the investigator, because I was saying that I was 14 when I was captured, because I had to. I emphasise that I had to lie because they were separating children of 16 years of age and killing them. And that is why. I had to say that I was 14, and then most probably this is where the misunderstanding occurred. I don't see any problem there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The part that I've just read out for you, is it truthful and accurate as to the events --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, if you want to draw our attention to this inconsistency with the previous statement and to the explanation that the witness has given, that is clear to the Chamber by now, unless there is any specific follow-up that you need to address instead of going over the same ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Agreed. Can I just ask one more question on this before moving on to another topic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that the SIPA investigator that interviewed you in this 2009 statement was speaking with you in your native language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now if we look at the latter half of paragraph 4. If we can -- I apologise. If we can back to 1D1097, and again not broadcast the same to the public. It should be page 4 in both versions. And again we're looking at the latter half of paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will omit names of individuals so as to protect you, but you can follow along with me, sir. It's at the bottom half of paragraph 4 and it starts off: "I heard from a soldier I knew that chemical agents were dropped on us, and I saw when a helicopter leaned to one side and dropped blue powder that fell on us. I did not know what this was, but my neighbour," and then you say his name, "who disappeared after the fall of Srebrenica, told me to cover my face and eyes. I left the place later, but," and then you mention the neighbour, "stayed behind and I never saw him again. They dropped the powder several times." Was this part of your statement to the SIPA investigator truthful and accurate as to its depiction of these events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I don't recall that statement. I tried the whole time to clarify that, to clear it up, to remember it. I don't remember that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the witness already testified, "Yes, I was there, but I don't remember the war agents, but I do remember everything else." So that he doesn't remember at this moment was already clear from his previous portion of his evidence. If there's any follow-up, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I want to know about the helicopters. Did you in fact personally see and eyewitness helicopters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. I don't remember. I cannot remember. I already tried. I told you, I don't recall the helicopters or them dropping any of those agents. As I said, I really did try to remember, but I just could not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness earlier today testified: "I don't remember the helicopters or anything like that. I don't remember them flying over us. I tried to remember that, but really, I cannot." Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now if we can have number 29070 in e-court. And if we can have page 11 of the English and page 15 of the B/C/S. It starts at line 25 in the English. It starts at line 4 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- and in relation to this you were asked about this incident, and you answered in -- it's either 2010 or 2011, I forgot now, as follows: "There were many people killed during the ambush, and the helicopter was flying above us calling for surrender. They told us, 'Come out, surrender. We are carrying food.' And some people did come out and they shot at them. I was with a neighbour of mine there on that location, and he told me 'They're throwing some poisonous substances on us,' and he said," and we should go to the next page in English, "'these people are not from Tuzla. Those are the Serbs. Those are the enemies.' So I listened to what my neighbour told me and I stayed put. I lay on the ground." Is this section that I've just read truthful and accurate as to the events that are depicted therein, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, no. I just told you I don't recall the helicopters. I don't remember that at all. I only remember the ambush. I remember that many people were killed in the ambush. That is something that I remember. As for the helicopters, I cannot remember that because I tried to remember that, but I really cannot. I'm sorry, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, can I ask you the following question: It was not that long ago that you gave those statements or gave that testimony. It is, well, I would say quite important, helicopters, chemical agents. Do you have any explanation as to why you have no recollection today on these events, whereas not that long ago and long after the events themselves you testified positive on those matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. The whole time in order to be 100 per cent that it did happen, I tried to remember that, to go over it, but please believe me, I cannot remember 100 per cent that this happened, that this did occur there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you not have similar doubts when you gave these statements, which again is a number of years ago but not that many, or did you have doubts already at that time as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. At that time I also had the doubts when I talked about it. It was at -- perhaps it happened, think about it a bit more. However, I could not remember. I should not have given those statements. I should not have given the statements, because I was not 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, we've been talking about the helicopters. I want to ask you about this neighbour. Do you recall if, in fact, you were lying on the ground and listening to what your neighbour described to you was happening? Do you remember that part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I only remember that we lay on the ground. We heard shooting from all sides, so we all lay down. That's all I can remember, nothing else. I just know that there was shooting all around us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
