utterances.text: Okay. So in your Rule 92 ter statement when you give us details about things that were happening during the shooting, are those things that you saw and eyewitnessed, or are those things that perhaps your neighbour told you while you were lying on the ground?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sorry, it's just not clear what things are being referred to here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you please be as precise as possible in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Paragraph 3 of the Rule 92 ter statement. I can read it so we don't have to pull it up in e-court: "During the night of 13 July, 1996," which was corrected from 1995, "we were ambushed. A beech tree was felled and them the ambush started from all sides. All types of weapons were used: Rifles, bombs, hand grenades, mines, and war agents. When we all dispersed I was separated from my father and I did not see him again after that." Then further found it talks about the helicopter -- told people there was food for them and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could we first try to go to the first part, because the remaining part I think the witness has been clear about that. All that what Mr. Ivetic has read to you a minute ago, that is about the start of the ambush, the beech tree being felled, all types of weapons were used, rifles, hand grenades, that you were with your father and that you didn't see him after that, is there any of that where you have any doubts as whether that is fully in accordance with what you remember? So I'm not talking about the helicopters. I'm not talking about the chemical agents, but weapons, beech tree, start of the ambush, types of weapons, you being there with your father.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You confirm that that is the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was there with my father when that happened, when this beech tree fell and when the shooting began at the spot where we were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry this wasn't pulled up for the witness and the witness had in fact already answered that question and qualified the reference to war agents. So I'm not -- Mr. Ivetic did read the entire sentence, but in the follow-up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I stopped him there, as a matter of fact, because that seemed to be the portion where the witness, as far as I understood him today, sticked very much to his story; whereas the following part that he had already withdrawn -- withdrawn from that. So that's the reason why I didn't want to mix it all up but to have it separate.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted that to be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But when I say "please proceed," perhaps I should have looked at the clock and announced that we will take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break. Could we go into closed session in order to allow the witness to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe I have not yet tendered 1D1097, the 2009 statement to SIPA into evidence. I would do so at this time under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, no objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1097 receives number D322, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D322 is admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to take you back to Kravica warehouse. In your statement you have now identified that ten people were executed in front of the warehouse and one kid was wounded, and that is how the 1997 statement to AID, which is D321, says there was a group of seven to ten captives that were shot. I'm not so concerned about this number. The question I want to ask you, sir, is: In relation to this incident, did you see one group? Is that accurate? Only one group in total that was executed of either ten or seven to ten, depending on which statement we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The group that had been brought there. I don't know how many men there were. There were some seven to ten. They were shot immediately, executed immediately, and while I was still there and present, they kept bringing people out of the hangar and executing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to ask you about because it's not in your statement, it's not in your 1997 statement, but it appears in your 2009 statement which is now D322 at paragraph 8 of the same, and I'd like to ask you what transpired between 1996, 1997, and 2009 that caused you to all of a sudden remember that there were multiple groups of persons that you saw being executed outside of Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I went and visited that place in Kravica, and thinking about it and looking at all that I recalled all the events and every wall where they took people out and shot them in front of those walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did that cause you to not remember that you saw multiple groups of persons executed? Is that what you're trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, did he say multiple groups or did he say the one group and then people had being taken out of the warehouse one by one and being executed?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. Perhaps we should do it in order. I'm trying to short-circuit for time but we should do it in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand, but let's not mislead witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you, sir, to clarify for us. Did you see multiple groups being taken out, or did you see additional people had been taken out? Could you clarify for us? Give us as much detail as you can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that first group that had been brought there. It was executed immediately, and after that they took people out of the hangar in tens, in groups of ten or so approximately. Then they would line them up against the wall and shoot them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how many additional groups of ten persons did you eyewitness being executed in front of the Kravica warehouse in addition to the one group of ten which is contained in your Rule 92 ter statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember precisely how many groups were taken out after the wounding of (redacted). I was frightened and all of that, so I wasn't really paying attention any more how many people were being brought out from the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In your 2009 statement to SIPA, which is now D322, you indicated that you remembered at least three groups of about ten men were taken out while you were there. Does that refresh your recollection or assist you in terms of helping us out here to find out how many groups in addition to the one group that you have testified to today were taken out and executed at the Kravica warehouse while you were present and watching?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It could be two or three groups, but I really don't remember. In my fright and the state that I was in, I cannot remember exactly how many groups were executed there. All I know is that people were being killed there, that people were being executed near the hangar. They were placed against the wall and shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now the question I have for you is to go back to that point where I asked you what transpired between 1996 and 2009 to cause you to all of a sudden remember all these additional details?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Counsel has the internal memorandum of an interview that was conducted with the witness in 2003 with the OTP, and in that interview the witness did mention people being taken out of the warehouse and executed, and that predates the 2009 statement that's being referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the Chamber is not aware of it, but if it caused you to rephrase your question and want to further look at the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was also going to say, Mr. Ivetic, you asked that same question a few minutes ago and the witness said he visited the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that's what I wanted to find out, why he visited that place. That's all. I was just trying to find that out, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When did you visit the location at Kravica when you said you looked at the walls where these people were killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in Kravica recently. I was there recently. I visited that place, so I did remember many of those things that happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you say "recently," are we talking as far back as 2003 or sometime after 2003?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm talking about this year, recently, perhaps I went a couple of months ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have anything that happened prior to a couple of months ago that caused you to remember these additional groups of persons taken out from the hangar and executed that you've now confirmed that is contained in your 2009 SIPA statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I saw some broadcasts once on television, and I could see people going through the woods escaping. I saw the hangar, and I remembered many things there, the things that I went through there. So part of that whole story came back to me while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now this is where I have a -- where I'm confused truly. Today you were presented this statement that only talked of one group. You were presented with a set of clarifications and corrections which is now P1689 under seal, which was supposed to correct anything that was wrong or incomplete in the first statement, and you have no mention of this additional -- of these additional groups that were taken out and executed. If you know this, if you believe it to be true, why did you not raise it during the Prosecution's examination of you today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I did say that other than those ten people who were executed, they kept taking people out of the hangar. I'm not sure about the number of the groups, because I don't know how many groups were taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it your belief that you said that today to the Prosecution or now to me when I was -- when I raised that issue with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I told you that answer just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I agree sir, and I confirmed that. Now, my question was: Why did you not raise it with the Prosecution during their examination of you today when they were talking about statement and any corrections to the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps I didn't understand the question in the best way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I think the matter you have raised is at least clear to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to 1D1096, and that also should not be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you will see, sir, this is dated 2003, 13 November. It is an internal memorandum of the Office of the Prosecutor relating to an interview that they had with you. Do you recall having an interview with members of the Prosecution staff in 2003, the month of November?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And it says here in the first paragraph to a large extent he remembered and confirmed the content of his statement which he made when he was 16 years of age. I'd like to -- let's see if I can find it. In the fourth paragraph from the top, you talk about -- well, strike that. This is what is recorded there. I should read it since there is no B/C/S: "There was a dead girl by the road. I walked round and round her. I lost my mind there, and I fled into forest. Someone fired at me but missed. I met a small group of BiH soldiers, and we went to Burnice near Konjevic Polje and found the village was full of BiH soldiers. There were about 500 of them. They had about 200 to 300 hunting weapons between them. There were old and young people there. They very hungry and were eating wild apples and other fruit." Does this accurately comport truthfully to your recollections and what you would have told the Prosecutors in November 2003 what actually happened in Burnice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember that. All I remember is that the girl was on the lower part -- in the lower part of the hangar, and I went round and round there. It could not have been above the road. I'm talking about the water, where that water was, and that's where I fled from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me be more specific. Is it accurate that the 500 persons in Burnice had 200 to 300 hunting weapons between them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that. I gave an approximate figure. I'm not sure about the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fair enough. Now, the second paragraph from the top says that -- this is again before you reached Kravica when you were separated from the group, separated from your father. It says: "I came close to Kravica. I think I was behind it. I found wounded people there. I was with them for two days. Some of them were committing suicide rather than waiting for the Chetniks to come. Does this section that I've read comport truthfully and accurately to your knowledge and recollection of the time period before you came to Kravica when you were behind Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This happened in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It did happen that people were killing themselves, people who were wounded, who could not walk by themselves, that they would do that. This is something that I saw in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now I'd like to move to the second page of this document and I'd like to present you the first two paragraphs, and since I've not received the B/C/S of this, I'll have to read it for you and ask you to following along, sir: "All four of us boys were taken to the kitchen at the barracks in Bratunac, and we were given pieces of meat to eat. I was afraid to eat, they cursed us, and we were kept in a small dark room. There was someone else in the room. I was afraid he was there to kill us. The man said he had been arrested and would be exchanged." Now, before I read the next part, sir, is it clear here that we're talking about the time period when you would have been in Bratunac after being captured the second time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When we came to Bratunac, we were taken straight to the kitchen and he cut off a piece of meat and he said, Eat. We said, We're not hungry. Then he said, Go to sleep then, you Balijas. And then they took us to a room somewhere over there and shut us in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The next morning you were taken for interrogation. I believe you mention that briefly in passing in direct examination. Do you recall anything about the identity or the appearance of the individual who you say examined you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was heavier, balding with brown hair, and he introduced himself by saying, I am Mladic. Perhaps it was somebody else. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And that's what I want to ask you. I would like to read this section to you from the document we have in front of us: "In the morning we were taken for interrogation. First all four of us went together when we were taken separately -- then we were taken separately. We were taken to an office and Ratko Mladic was there with four other soldiers. He asked if I knew who he was. I didn't and he told me. He asked me where the BiH Army was and what the BiH Army was eating in the forest. I told him they were eating snails, and he was very -- he was angry with his soldiers. He said, Why can't you beat this army? You have meals and they are eating snails. Ratko Mladic said that he was not a child killer. I am sure it was Ratko Mladic, because he introduced himself to us." And I'd like to ask you, first of all, does this comport truthfully and accurately to your recollection of the facts so that -- of this -- of this encounter, this part I've read out to you from the internal memorandum of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he introduced himself as Ratko Mladic. I didn't know the man. I don't know whether it was really Ratko Mladic or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was that on the same day that you were taken to be exchanged to the free Muslim territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember whether that was on the same day or after we spent the night. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, how many days did you spend in Bratunac before being put in the white car that was marked UNPROFOR and being taken first to the police station and then to the exchange?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember how many days we spent in Bratunac. I cannot remember. We were frightened and all that. I couldn't remember. I cannot remember those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is there any reason why this detail, this critical detail of an encounter you claimed to have had with General Mladic was not mentioned previously in any of your prior statements or any of your prior testimonies and is only mentioned in this internal memorandum from 2003?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. No one asked me about that. We did not talk about the exchange anymore. All they asked me is where we came or where -- where was the point where we reached the free territory. I said it was Kalesija. I don't remember if anyone asked me whether it was Ratko Mladic or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Have you -- having now had the opportunity to be in this courtroom with my client, can you state if you have ever met my client who is in this courtroom prior to today's date in person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that. I cannot remember. It's been many years since then. People change a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask that this document be introduced as the next exhibit number under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections? Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1096 receives number D323, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask the witness to take off his earphones for a second. Thank you. Mr. Ivetic, just for my understanding you're tendering this document mainly in view of inconsistency of statements or for the truth of its content or -- it's not entirely clear to me what, because some nice things are said about Mr. Mladic as well in the statement. So I'm just wondering what -- what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Inconsistencies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Inconsistency, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Inconsistency. Only inconsistent or also not truthful?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's for Your Honours to decide. I believe that the testimony is not reliable --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the position -- yes. The position of the Defence is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- put it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- he was not interviewed by Mr. Mladic at that point in time at that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me then -- then the number, Madam Registrar, has already been assigned. D323 is admitted into evidence under seal. Could the witness put his earphones on again. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the next series of questions I think we need to go into private session to protect the identity of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can call up P1689 but not broadcast the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, this is the corrections provided by yourself to the Office of the Prosecutor to the statement that we have -- to the 92 ter statement which we have introduced into evidence, and I want to look at the last paragraph on the first page of both versions, both languages, and that reads -- that's the part that is regarding paragraph 10 of your statement, saying: "Regarding the sentence reading, '... in the field were about 500 corpses lying all over it,' the witness stated that he may have mentioned the figure of 500 at the time. He gave this statement as this was his first impression. He did see a lot of bodies but not as many as 500." Now, today I think you have said approximately 100, and whether we're talking about a lot of bodies or 100 bodies, were they all in one place or were they scattered out throughout several locations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all over the field where we were brought. They were killed all over the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that the bodies that you saw did not have their hands tied in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I don't know. I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now in your Rule 92 ter statement you've talked about some trenches. And can you tell me were these battle trenches? Were they canals? What were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They were canals. Perhaps they were there from before. I don't know if they were already there from having been dug out before. All I know is that they were already there in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There were no machines or personnel digging them. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. No, there were no people digging. We found the bodies already in the field. They were already there when we got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'd like to briefly look at 65 ter number 29070, and again not broadcast the same. Page 23 in English, page 26 in the B/C/S. And here you're being asked about -- it's at paragraph -- it's at page -- line 21 in the B/C/S and line 15 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You're being asked about the bodies in the field in this -- in this testimony and your answer is recorded as follows: "There were bodies that -- when you glance over the meadow, when you look around yourself and you see a meadow and there were bodies scattered on the meadow. So that's how I can put it, body here and a body there." And is that truthful and accurate as to your recollections of how the bodies in the field were visible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were bodies strewn on the meadow when we came. They were not all in one heap. It seemed as though they were fleeing and were killed. The bodies were scattered throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say it seemed that they were fleeing and were killed, would that mean that the bodies were individual bodies rather than groups of bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact number, but there were people, bodies, scattered through the meadow. Wherever you looked, there were bodies on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now I'd like to take a look at 65 ter number 29071, and if we can have page 14 in the English but not broadcast the same -- pardon me, not page 14. Page 29 in the English and page 42 in the B/C/S. Actually, it's going to be page 43 in the B/C/S. And it's going to actually be like the next page in English. I'm trying to short-circuit most of this. The next page in English. And it's just above the middle of the payment, the first quarter of the page that I am going to be asking about. Sir, in this -- I will read for you as follows how the testimony is recorded: "Defence counsel: Next you say that those bodies were in front of 10 or 15 trenches, each 1 metre wide and 1 metre deep, half filled with water and the trenches were dug here as you said. Does this refresh your memory? Was it like that or were they in the road unclear as you said today? "The witness: Well, that is a meadow, yes. There were trenches crossing the meadow, but how many trenches exactly, maybe I did say 10 or 15. Maybe I said three, you understand, because I know that there were trenches where I was lying and in front of me and behind me that there were three trenches. "Defence counsel: Do you agree that what you said today differs from what you said in 1996? "The witness: It must be different. I am saying three or four trenches today and there it says 10 trenches, 13." Does this section that I've read out to you from the prior testimony accurately and truthfully comport to our recollection of how you testified in that trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I remember that there were some trenches dug out and that there were people killed on the meadow, but other than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the trenches were by the road and there were three of them that you recall? Is that how you testified in this case -- pardon me, in that case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember that. As I have said, not to repeat myself, I just remember the trenches that had been dug out. It had been done before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, before we continue, I would like to ask Ms. Hasan whether her position has changed in any way as far as re-examination is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have two very brief matters which shouldn't take more than three to four minutes to cover.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'm addressing you, Mr. Ivetic. Where are we at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender the documents -- I apologise. The documents 29070 and 29071 in their entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It means the whole of the proceedings, is that or is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Only the witness's testimony. It's not the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 29070 receives number D324, Your Honours. And document 29071 receives number D325, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, you're not jumping up. May I take it therefore that there's no objection. D324 and D325 are admitted under seal. Mr. Ivetic, I return to my question where we stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I should be able to conclude in a matter of, let's say, seven minutes. And I'll rely upon the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Seven minutes plus -- I would then keep you to that. That means you have until 2.35 and then you have another five minutes, Ms. Hasan. And this is all possible due to the co-operation of all those assisting us in and around the courtroom. Your seven minutes start now, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to call up D321. Which hopefully should be 1D1095. Yes. If we can have page 2 in the English and also page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, the part I'm referring to is the first full paragraph in the B/C/S that says [B/C/S spoken]. And I'd like to read the English and ask you some questions about it: "After this the Chetniks ordered my group which numbered about 10 to 12 people to get up and they gave each one of us an automatic rifle and two ammunition magazines and told us to go towards the centre of the village of Kravica with the rifles, because Ejub Golic was allegedly supposed to appear with his group and we were to open fire at them. We walked down the asphalt road from the warehouse in a line and fanned out. While the Chetniks, about 20 of them, walked behind us with their rifles cocked telling us that they would kill us if we did not open fire on our people. As we walked like that towards the centre of Kravica at a distance of about 50 metres from the warehouse we were ordered to turn right from the main asphalt road towards the woods where we stopped for a rest. Then one Chetniks took out an empty plastic bottle." And I'd like to ask you about that. First of all, is it correct that 10 to 12 of you were given rifles and armed by the Bosnian Serbs at Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We were given rifles in front of the hangar, but as far as I remember, we went down towards the river, not far from the hangar. We didn't stay there long and then returned back to the hangars.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. The question I have for you, sir, is, first of all, in the two ammunition magazines that you were given, how many bullets? I presume there were bullets. Were the guns loaded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't know whether the guns were loaded, whether they were operational or not. That was my first encounter with weapons whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This statement that we have in front of us right now says that immediately after you stopped at the forest to take a rest, that the one soldier gave you an empty bottle to go fill it up with water, and so the question I have for you is: Is this accurate that you were not at the warehouse when you were given the bottle of water and told to go fill it up but that you were, rather, at this other position taking a rest after patrolling the territory looking for this Muslim unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We were by the hangars and I remember well that we went down the road towards the river and then spent some time there, and once we returned it is then that he gave us the bottle to fetch some water.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm told the French a coming through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You receive B/C/S again, Mr. Mladic? Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I want to talk about the girl that was at the water hose with her throat slit. In your ICTY statement, you identify the girl as being dead when you saw her, but in the trials in Bosnia, in one you say the body was still shaking, and in the other one you say that in fact she was still alive and breathing her last breath. Which of these is the full truth, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the full truth. When I came to that girl, she was shaking. She was about to die but not dead yet, and upon seeing that I started running away from the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With -- with regard to the rifle that you were given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could I ask one question? Mr. Witness, did you see that girl, her throat being slit by someone, or did you just see her lying on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. When I came, because I'd been sent to fetch water, she was there near the water, and as I passed by, she was shaking. She was about to die. There was blood all over her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you see anyone near or close to her who would have slit her throat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I don't remember seeing anybody close to her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At the time that you and approximately ten other individuals were armed with rifles that had two ammunition magazines each, was this the same time outside of Kravica warehouse when you claim that groups of persons were being taken out and being executed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It was taking place there at the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is it your testimony that none of you of the 10 or 12 persons that had rifles in their hands did anything to try to stop these persons from taking out multiple groups of people and executing them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I'm looking at the clock. We are now at eight minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. I'm done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're done. Thank you for that. Ms. Hasan, you needed a few minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we please have D322 called up, and this is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, you recall a discussion earlier today about whether or not you gave an incorrect age to the investigator of SIPA, which is the State Investigation and Prosecution Agency in the Ministry of Security in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you recall that discussion, and you explained there was a misunderstanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we turn to page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And it reads under item 4, "You are obliged to give the following information about yourself," and this is once the interview had already began, and, Witness, there is information there about your name, your parents' name, et cetera, et cetera. Did you provide this information which included date of birth as recorded on that page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Witness, there are several individuals that you've specifically named in your 1996 statement that we discussed earlier today that you gave to the ICTY. You recall those individuals I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you said these -- you saw these individuals at the meadow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And that was the last time that you saw them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you saw these persons, were they alive at the time or were they dead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The people there were alive. If you have in mind the people whose names I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes. The ones --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Perhaps we can pull it up real quick to confirm. P1690. This is also under seal. And if we could very quickly turn to page 5, paragraph 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay, Witness. You see the -- take a look at the first paragraph that appears on your screen. You see the names that you mention there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So are these the individuals that you've just confirmed were alive when you last saw them at the meadow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just one, Your Honour, arising from those two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We have 322 up on the screen. If we can go to page 5 in both versions. Oh, I apologise. This is the statement. If we can go to D322, page 5 in both versions, and focus on the end of paragraph 7. And of course not broadcast the same since it's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You were asked about the misunderstanding as to the age from the statement, and I want to point to the last line of this where you're talking about the individual who was wounded, and you indicate that he was a year younger than you and that he was 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't ask him about the misunderstanding. He already explained --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's not be over-formalistic. Mr. Ivetic, you wanted to draw our attention to the fact that by referring to that person as being one year younger and therefore being 13 that that would also underline that the witness stated that he was 14 at the time. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I was going to ask him if he could explain that, but if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, could I briefly try. You referred to the person wounded, the boy. You said he was a year younger than you, so he was 13. There again, you suggest that you were 14 at the time, but it's difficult to understand that as being misunderstanding, because you -- you're saying it yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He went to school with me. We were in the same class. We had -- we were of equal age. If I lied about the age, I said he was 13 and I was 14, I had to do that because I'd been taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't say I was 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was part of sticking to your own story -- to the old story that you were 14.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. It's been clarified. Witness, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for answering all the questions that were put to you by the parties and the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again. We will -- after you've left the courtroom, once we're in closed session, we will adjourn for the day and resume on Friday, the 5th of July, at 9.30 in the morning in this same Courtroom III, but we'll then resume in open session, I take it, depending on any protective measures which we have to verify. Then we -- I would first like to thank all those who made it possible to conclude the testimony of this witness today, that is security, interpreters, transcribers, everyone who assisted in achieving this. We turn into closed session.
